subject: GPU price-spike buffer approval & emergency capacity playbook - Nimbus Labs
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU price-spike buffer ask for Nimbus (HB-4821)

Team —

Quick summary: Nimbus wants to close this week. They signed on to a 24-month reserved capacity commitment for Dedicated (large enterprise profile) but added a hard ask: an emergency price-spike buffer clause that reduces unit discounts if market GPU spot indices jump >15% month-over-month. They expect predictable uptime and want us to cap their unit price exposure.

Why this matters now:
- Deal is $1.8M ARR committed over 24 months (attached proposal).
- Our current SKU mix for Nimbus assumes A100-equivalent pricing at our negotiated vendor rates. A near-term GPU spot shock would materially change our margin if we commit without guardrails.

Request: I need a short internal approval path and a recommended clause we can offer that balances customer protection with our margin exposure. Ideally we provide:
1) A one-time "buffer" credit applied if GPU spot spike >15% for two consecutive months (cap credits to X% of committed spend), OR
2) A trigger allowing temporary SKU rebalancing (swap lower-cost quantized variants) with customer notification.

I've attached the capacity model and latest proposal. Marcus, can you run a 3-scenario sensitivity (base / +20% / +40% GPU cost) and recommend a credit cap that keeps EBITDA impact <2%? Kimberly, can you advise whether Legal/Finance will accept a documented trigger mechanics (index reference, notice window, mitigation steps) vs a blanket price pass-through? Laura, loop-in CS if we need to bake operational fallbacks.

Short timeline — Nimbus is pushing for signature by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU price-spike buffer ask for Nimbus (HB-4821)

Sean / team —

Attached a quick sensitivity workbook (capacity_model.xlsx) with three scenarios. Top-line:
- Base: expected margin headroom 14% on the committed SKU mix.
- +20% GPU cost: headroom drops to ~6.5%.
- +40% GPU cost: headroom goes negative (~-3%).

Recommendations (finance-first):
- Offer a conservative credit cap at 8% of quarterly committed spend for a single declared spike window. This keeps expected blended margin >5% under +20% stress.
- For sustained shocks (>2 months), allow SKU rebalancing to a quantized variant with a documented performance delta tolerance (we should publish approximate latency/accuracy deltas to the customer).
- Use a reputable market index (e.g., CloudVendor GPU spot index) with a one-month lookback, and require a 10-business-day notice from Redwood before credits are auto-applied.

I'll mark cells with sensitivity assumptions and include a short note about amortizing credits vs one-off offsets.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 13:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU price-spike buffer ask for Nimbus (HB-4821)

Sean / Marcus —

Legal & Pricing POV: we prefer a deterministic trigger + mitigation path rather than an open-ended credit. Key points Legal will insist on:
- Explicit index definition (single source) and how it's measured.
- Cap on cumulative credits over the term (suggest 12% total of committed value).
- A requirement that Redwood must first attempt mitigation (SKU swap, temporary throttles, prefix caching) before crediting the customer.
- A clause that preserves SLAs for uptime but allows temporary performance tiering with customer consent (documented in rollback/notifications).

Proposed customer-facing clause (brief):
"In the event that the Redwood GPU Spot Index exceeds the baseline by greater than 15% for two consecutive billing cycles, Redwood may, at its discretion, offer (i) a one-time usage credit not to exceed 8% of the then-current quarter's committed spend, or (ii) implement temporary SKU rebalancing to preserve service continuity. Any credits issued shall not exceed a cumulative 12% of total contracted value over the Term. Redwood will provide at least 10 business days' notice prior to issuing credits or changing SKU mix."

If Nimbus requires a lower cap, we'll need exec approval. From Pricing side, 8% one-time / 12% cap is a workable default.

Kimberly
VP, Pricing & Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Arya Kapoor <arya@nimbus.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GPU price-spike buffer approval & emergency capacity playbook - Nimbus Labs

Sean —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for sharing the proposed clause. Nimbus is generally comfortable with a trigger-based approach, but procurement has two asks before we sign:
1) The one-time credit should be set at 10% of quarterly committed spend (they want slightly more buffer).
2) For transparency, we request monthly reporting on SKU changes and a post-event review if a credit is applied.

If Redwood can accept 10% one-time, and we keep your 12% cumulative cap, we can sign this week. Please confirm and send a clean redline.

Best,
Arya Kapoor
Head of Cloud Ops — Nimbus Labs
arya@nimbus.ai
